hints: Follow the ball thrown up until it is back at the top of the tower. How is it moving then, compared with the other ball at the start?
worded:
1. The ball thrown up at 10 m/s rises, stops and falls back. By symmetry it passes the top of the tower again after 2 s, moving down at 10 m/s.

2. From then on it is in exactly the situation the second ball was in at the start: at the top, moving down at 10 m/s.

3. So it repeats the second ball’s journey, just 2 s late. The difference is 2 s, whatever the height of the tower. (B)

**No-pen route.** The answer is the time to go up and come back: 2u/g = 2 s. The 200 m is not needed.
conventional:
![](asset:P000111-sol-1)

Take up as positive and the top of the tower as origin; the ground is at $y = - 200$ m.

Ball thrown up: $- 200 = 10t_{1} - 5t_{1}^{2}$, so $t_{1}^{2} - 2t_{1} - 40 = 0$ and $t_{1} = 1 + \sqrt{41}$ s.

Ball thrown down: $- 200 = - 10t_{2} - 5t_{2}^{2}$, so $t_{2}^{2} + 2t_{2} - 40 = 0$ and $t_{2} = - 1 + \sqrt{41}$ s.

$$t_{1} - t_{2} = 2\unit{s} = \frac{2u}{g}.$$
mistakes: No need to solve two quadratics: the difference is just the extra up-and-back time, 2u/g.
Both balls hit the ground with the same speed; only their times differ.
